title: Reading the bill: on demand, Savings Plans and Reserved Instances

videos.script: One machine in São Paulo. The same machine, the same hour. And three different prices. {{three}} On demand, you pay the full rate, and you promise nothing. With a reservation, you promise to pay for that type of machine every hour for a year. With a Savings Plan, you promise to spend so many dollars an hour on computing. {{table}} The promise buys a discount of about a third. But the promise is paid every hour, whether the machine runs or not. {{breakeven}} So the question is never how big the discount is. It is how many hours the machine really runs. Below a certain number, the promise loses money. {{lines}} Then the lesson opens the bill itself. One hour can be one line, two lines, or three, depending on how it was paid. Read them wrong, and you count the same hour twice. {{wrong}} Last, a bill that arrived at twice the expected size. Not one of the extra lines is a machine. Every price in this lesson comes from AWS's published list, read by a program you run yourself. {{end}}
